text:
aisha: Heads up — since ~01:40Z we've seen ~6% GPU attach failures in eu-west3. Noticing attach latencies spike and some pods stuck in ContainerCreating for >2m.

Tom: ugh, is this the nightly scrub again?

aisha: digging — node metrics show ephemeral-cleaner IO ops jumping from ~3.8k -> 14k when janitor starts. GPU attach flows hit iowait and kubelet times out on volume attach.

lucas: confirmed on my side — stack traces show NVME_reads backlog and iostat -> 
```
Device:        rrqm/s wrqm/s   r/s   w/s  rMB/s  wMB/s avgrq-sz avgqu-sz await r_await w_await svctm  %util
nvme0n1         0.00  10.00  80.0  420.0   8.1   12.3    62.0    21.4  45.0   20.1  47.6  1.95  82.3
```

storage-bot: ALERT: ephemeral-cleaner:iops_spike eu-west3 (2026-03-21T01:41Z) - 14.2k ops, avg_latency 42ms :rotating_light:

maya: that's bad — Dedicated customers in that region saw warm anomalies last week. We need a mitigation ASAP.

Tom: short-term mitigation idea: throttle janitor concurrency to 2 on eu-west3 for next 2 hours. There's a dirty flag in configsvc: `janitor.concurrent_jobs` — we can patch rollout via platform-config.

lucas: I can push a quick patch. Plan: set janitor.concurrent_jobs=2 in configsvc cluster config; then bump back after we verify attach success. Command: `kubectl -n infra exec deploy/configsvc -- sh -c "cfg set janitor.concurrent_jobs 2 && cfg reload"` — test on canary nodes first.

aisha: before we do that, can we also add a warmup coordinator so janitors don't all start at top of hour? If we stagger starts by node label windows (0-5m, 5-10m, etc.) we should flatten the IO curve.

lucas: Agreed — medium term we should implement a janitor-coordinator. Quick script I ran to assign windows: `for n in $(nodes -l zone=europe-west3); do label=$(( (RANDOM % 6) * 5 )); kubectl label node $n janitor-window=${label}m --overwrite; done` — then janitor respects label and delays startup.

maya: note tradeoff — lowering concurrency increases scrub completion time which could push more work into maintenance windows and slightly increase storage write amplification (cost). But it's acceptable for a 2h emergency.

Tom: go for the patch + label-stagger. Lucas — can you do patch on canary in 5 mins and target all eu-west3 if green? Aisha — can you notify SRE and CS (oncall) that Dedicated traffic may see brief recovery window?

lucas: deploying to canary now. `kubectl -n infra rollout restart deploy/configsvc` -> applying config change.

storage-bot: CONFIG PATCH: configsvc janitor.concurrent_jobs set to 2 in cluster eu-west3-canary (deploy by lucas) at 2026-03-21T01:46Z

lucas: canary looks good — attach success rate back to 98% within 30s. Rolling to eu-west3 region now.

aisha: labeling nodes to stagger starts now. small script run, pushed labels to 60% nodes.

maya: pinging billing — if we run stagger+lower concurrency for 4h, estimated additional IO window cost ~+0.8% for the fleet in region (rough calc). I'll log to the incident ticket.

Tom: excellent. Post-mortem actions: 1) implement janitor-coordinator feature to stagger by default, 2) add rate-limit knob exposed per-region, 3) add runbook step to throttle janitor via configsvc. I'll create tickets.

aisha: open ticket INFRA-4239, linking logs and metrics. Oncall to monitor attach success and NVME util for 2h. Thanks team. :thumbsup:

lucas: leaving a follow-up note — we should also consider a KV cache for janitor workload to avoid rewalking huge directories during restart which spikes IO. Low priority but will shave ops.

storage-bot: MONITOR: eu-west3 nvme_util down to 54% at 2026-03-21T01:58Z, attach success 99.3%

Tom: closing loop — if things remain green at 02:30Z we revert config to normal concurrency and keep staggering labels for the week.

maya: added cost note to INFRA-4239 and CCed CS.

aisha: thanks, closing thread — will paste postmortem when done.
